question: Assume today is 2026-08-23. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of live births in South Korea in July 2026, as it will be first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Population Trends release.

target.what: Number of live births occurring in South Korea during July 2026, as first reported in Statistics Korea's monthly Population Trends (인구동향) release
target.publisher: Statistics Korea (KOSTAT), monthly Population Trends / 인구동향
target.cadence: monthly, typically released ~2 months after the reference month (provisional)
target.caveats: Counts births by month of occurrence (occurrence basis), not registration date; provisional figures are later revised. Working interpretation: births occurring in July 2026 nationally (resident population), first provisional release. Alternative: births registered in July 2026 (registration basis) w

candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 births = July 2025 births adjusted by the recent year-on-year trend in monthly births; July has a distinct seasonal level relative to adjacent months.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly live birth counts for South Korea for each month of 2023, 2024, 2025 and any 2026 months published before cutoff (Jan-Jun 2026), plus July values for 2023-2025. Minimum: July 2025 count and the latest 12-month YoY growth rates.
search_hints: Statistics Korea monthly live births 2025 인구동향

candidates.hypothesis: Resident registration (주민등록) birth registrations and birth-related administrative counts track the statistics-agency birth series with a stable ratio and lag, allowing a bridge to the July 2026 occurrence count.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly 주민등록 출생자 수 (resident registration births) for 2025 and Jan-Jul 2026 from Ministry of Interior and Safety (행정안전부), and the historical ratio to KOSTAT monthly births.

candidates.hypothesis: National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) counts of births/deliveries (분만 건수) provide an independent monthly proxy for live births, bridged by the historical ratio of NHIS delivery claims to KOSTAT births.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly NHIS 분만(출산) 급여 건수 for 2025 and 2026 to date; historical ratio of NHIS delivery claims to KOSTAT live births.

candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 births ≈ women of childbearing age × age-specific fertility rates for July, or annual births × July seasonal share; the seasonal share of July within the year is stable.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly seasonal distribution of births (share of annual births in July) for 2020-2025, and any 2026 annual birth projection or year-to-date total to apply the share to.
search_hints: Korea monthly birth seasonality share July
South Korea births by month seasonal pattern

candidates.hypothesis: Published 2026 birth projections or year-to-date commentary (e.g., KOSTAT, Bank of Korea, research institutes) constrain the plausible July 2026 level and the direction of the 2026 trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Any 2026 annual or monthly birth forecasts, KOSTAT press commentary on 2026 monthly releases (Jan-Jun 2026), and reported YoY changes in early-2026 births.

candidates.hypothesis: Policy changes (e.g., expanded parental benefits, marriage/childbirth incentives) and calendar effects (lunar dates, holidays) shift monthly births; measurable exposure helps adjust the trend extrapolation.
candidates.data_to_find: Timing and scale of major 2024-2026 pronatalist policy expansions, marriage registration trends (marriages lead births by ~1-2 years), and any reported effect on 2025-2026 birth counts.
search_hints: Korea birth incentive policy 2025 2026 effect births

directions.hypothesis: Monthly NHIS 분만 (delivery) claim counts for Jan–Jun 2026, bridged by the 98.6% NHIS/KOSTAT ratio (p17), would give an independent July 2026 birth level and let us check whether the Q1 2026 surge (p29–p33) persisted into summer. This is the single most valuable missing input because it is the only route that does not rely on extrapolating the 2025 July level.
directions.data_to_find: NHIS monthly 분만자 수 or 분만 건수 for 2026 (at least April–June 2026), and the corresponding KOSTAT monthly births for the same months to re-estimate the bridge ratio.

directions.hypothesis: The July share of annual births and the July-vs-June and July-vs-August ratios in 2023–2025 would let us convert the strong Q1 2026 level into a July 2026 level without assuming the 2025 July YoY rate persists. July is typically a high-birth month (autumn conceptions), so a naive carry-forward of the Q1 growth rate may overstate July.
directions.data_to_find: KOSTAT monthly live births for July 2023, July 2024 (p36 gives 20,601), July 2025 (p1 gives 21,803), and the June/August neighbors, to compute the July seasonal index.

directions.hypothesis: Published 2026 birth projections or mid-2026 monthly commentary (e.g., KOSTAT Q2 2026 release, BOK, research institutes) would resolve whether the Q1 2026 +14.8% surge (p29–p31) moderated in Q2 — the key uncertainty in the trend-extrapolation route. If Q2 growth fell back toward single digits, July 2026 should be scaled down accordingly.
directions.data_to_find: KOSTAT Q2 2026 (April–June) monthly births and YoY rates; any 2026 annual birth forecast published before 2026-08-23.

methods.rationale: Direct trend extrapolation: July 2026 = July 2025 level (p1) times a YoY growth factor (a1) grounded in the 2026 Q1 surge (p29–p33) but moderated for the fading marriage tailwind (p26) and the high July 2025 base. methods.rationale: Seasonal-share decomposition: annual births (p16, 2024 = 238k) times July's share of the year (a2). This route is weaker because it uses the 2024 annual total rather than a 2026 estimate, so it implicitly assumes 2026 annual births are near 2024 levels — which understates the 2026 rebound. It is kept as a structural cross-check on the seasonal level rather than as a primary estimate. Failure mode: the 2026 annual total is materially above 238k, biasing this low.

assumptions.name: July 2026 YoY birth growth factor relative to July 2025
assumptions.rationale: July 2025 births were 21,803 (p1), up 5.9% (p2). The 2026 upswing is strong: Q1 2026 +14.8% (p31), March +19.4% (p33), February a 7-year high (p27). But the marriage leading indicator broke its 22-month streak in Feb 2026 (p26), and July 2025 was already a high base, so July 2026 growth should be positive but below the Q1 peak. A central 8% with a wide 10th–90th range of -2% to +20% reflects the fading-momentum risk and the possibility that the Q1 surge persists.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 birth rebound continues at a moderated pace through July; July 2026 is compared to the same calendar month in 2025.
assumptions.falsified_by: Q2 2026 monthly data showing growth collapsing to near zero or turning negative, or NHIS delivery counts for spring 2026 falling well below 2025 levels.

assumptions.name: July seasonal share of annual births
assumptions.rationale: July is a moderately high birth month in Korea (autumn conceptions). With ~238k annual births (p16) and July 2025 at 21,803 (p1), the July share is ≈ 21,803/238,000 ≈ 9.2%; using a slightly lower central value accounts for the 2026 annual total being higher than 2024's. The range spans typical July shares of 8.0–9.2%.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 annual birth total is known or estimated and July's seasonal share is stable across years.
assumptions.falsified_by: Monthly 2026 data showing July's share of the year deviating materially from the 2023–2025 range.
